title: Rigveda 8.58: Fragment
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 8.58: Fragment: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 8.58 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to fragment. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 8, the book of the Kaṇva and Aṅgiras poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 629r-629v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 8.58.1-2 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 4, varga 29); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 629r
translation.original_text:
1yam ṛ̱tvijo̍ bahu̱dhā ka̱lpaya̍nta̱ḥ sace̍taso ya̱jñam i̱maṁ vaha̍nti | yo a̍nūcā̱no brā̍hma̱ṇo yu̱kta ā̍sī̱t kā svi̱t tatra̱ yaja̍mānasya sa̱ṁvit ||
2eka̍ e̱vāgnir ba̍hu̱dhā sami̍ddha̱ eka̱ḥ sūryo̱ viśva̱m anu̱ prabhū̍taḥ | ekai̱voṣāḥ sarva̍m i̱daṁ vi bhā̱ty eka̱ṁ vā i̱daṁ vi ba̍bhūva̱ sarva̍m ||
translation.text:
1HE whom the priests in sundry ways arranging the sacrifice, of one accord, bring hither, Who was appointed as a learned Brahman, -what is the sacrificer's knowledge of him?
2Kindled in many a spot, still One is Agni; Sûrya is One though high o'er all he shineth. Illumining this All, still One is Ushas. That which is One hath into All developed.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 629r (numbered 51r by the scribe) (OPenn image 629, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 8.57.1 ‹-yajatrā ā agacchatam nāsatyā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 629v (numbered 51v by the scribe), begins in RV 8.58.3 ‹-jyotiṣmantam ketu-mantam tri-cakram su-kham›. Verses 8.58.1-2 end on this page.

2ekaḥ | eva | agniḥ | bahudhā | sam-iddhaḥ | ekaḥ | sūryaḥ | viśvam | anu | pra-bhūtaḥ | ekā | eva | uṣāḥ | sarvam | idam | vi | bhāti | ekam | vai | idam | vi | babhūva | sarvam

translation.original_ref: RV 8.58.3 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 4, varga 29); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 629v
translation.original_text: <sup>3</sup>jyoti̍ṣmantaṁ ketu̱manta̍ṁ trica̱kraṁ su̱khaṁ ratha̍ṁ su̱ṣada̱m bhūri̍vāram | ci̱trāma̍ghā̱ yasya̱ yoge̍ 'dhijajñe̱ taṁ vā̍ṁ hu̱ve ati̍ rikta̱m piba̍dhyai ||
translation.text: <sup>3</sup>The chariot bright and radiant, treasure-laden, three-wheeled, with easy seat, and lightly rolling, Which She of Wondrous Wealth was born to harness,– this car of yours I call. Drink what remaineth.
